plan.title: Organize the issue actions context menu into clear sections
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: The issue right-click menu (FeatureContextMenu in FeatureItem.tsx) flattens all 44 registry actions into one unlabeled list, appends three hardcoded extras (Open State Dir, View JSONL, a duplicate Deep Wipe with window.confirm), and mixes destructive operations with routine controls. The cockpit's action panel already ships an operator-proven grouping taxonomy (GROUP_ORDER/GROUP_LABELS in IssueMissionControl.tsx) that the registry does not own, so the two surfaces can drift.
narratives.Proposal: Follow PRD rev 2 (drafts/pan-2661.md) and the binding mockup exactly: (1) retire the orphaned reviewTest entry via the D-6 migration table; (2) move GROUP_ORDER/GROUP_LABELS into the shared registry (issueActions.ts) and add a required description field with the mockup appendix copy; (3) build a shared GroupedIssueActionMenu implementing the D-3 structure (phase header, 'For this phase', registry groups in order, 'This session' extras, collapsed Danger disclosure last) with an Explain toggle (D-5); (4) adopt it in FeatureContextMenu, deleting the flat dump and the hardcoded Deep Wipe after unifying the wipe body to {deleteWorkspace:true} (D-4); (5) lock everything with an extended parity test and a new FeatureContextMenu row in the PAN-2499 no-loss inventory.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to any enabledWhen gating predicate (issueActions.ts:137-195) — semantics stay byte-identical to useIssueActions.
- No registry promotion of Open State Dir / View JSONL / other surface extras — that is PAN-1610; here they render as sessionExtras props.
- No changes to dialog routing, confirm flows, or the IssueActionDialogHost mount.
- No new grouping taxonomy — the cockpit's existing groups are reused verbatim.
- No behavior changes beyond the two in the D-7 ledger (wipe unification, reviewTest migration); a third behavior change is out of spec.
- No cockpit IssueActionMegaMenu redesign — it only switches to the registry-exported GROUP_ORDER/GROUP_LABELS and gains description tooltips on enabled buttons.
- No Mintlify page for the context menu (none exists today; PRD + mockup are the design record).

autoDecisions.summary: Ran fully from PRD rev 2 + mockup spec appendix as binding inputs; no operator questions asked.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD is implementation-grade, operator-reviewed (rev 2 incorporates the gpt-5.6 feedback), and the issue comments confirm the approach. All PRD claims were re-verified against the current tree (post-PAN-2499).

autoDecisions.summary: reviewTest retirement (D-6) is sequenced BEFORE exporting the 8-group GROUP_ORDER from the registry.
autoDecisions.rationale: The cockpit's current GROUP_ORDER includes 'preserved' and renders reviewTest today. Exporting the binding 8-group order first would silently hide reviewTest before its migration lands — a no-loss violation. Retirement first also lets the IssueActionGroup union drop 'preserved' so the exported GROUP_LABELS record type covers exactly 8 groups.

autoDecisions.summary: spotlight.ts Tests-failed migration goes to restartReview, deviating from PRD D-6 clause (2) which names requestReview.
autoDecisions.rationale: IssueBlockerSpotlight filters to enabled actions only (IssueBlockerSpotlight.tsx:26), and canRequestReview requires !state.reviewStatus — false in every Tests-failed state — so requestReview would silently drop the re-run affordance, violating the issue's no-loss requirement. canRestartReview covers testStatus 'failed'/'dispatch_failed' exactly, preserving the affordance with a correct gate. The drawer-legacy 'Review & Test' parity-map rows still migrate to requestReview (same panVerb and endpoint as reviewTest).

autoDecisions.summary: Wipe body unification (bodyForAction('wipe') → {deleteWorkspace:true}) lands as its own item BEFORE the hardcoded Deep Wipe is deleted.
autoDecisions.rationale: Deleting the hardcoded item first would leave an interval where the only wipe path sends {} (no workspace deletion) — a silent capability regression. Landing the body first keeps every intermediate commit at-or-above today's behavior.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs gate satisfied by updating docs/ISSUE-VIEW.md in the inventory item rather than a docs-only item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD states (verified) that no Mintlify page documents the context menu; the genuinely documented surface is the issue-view no-loss inventory described in docs/ISSUE-VIEW.md, which gains the FeatureContextMenu row.

narrative.Action: Execute the D-6 migration table, one commit-reviewable row per consumer, then delete the entry. (1) ReviewVerificationCard.tsx:115-119 — replace the reviewTest lookup with recoverReview so actionButtons becomes [restartReview, recoverReview] filtered by .enabled (PRD product call: the card's purpose is re-running a failed/stuck review). (2) spotlight.ts:52 (Tests failed case) — replace 'reviewTest' with 'restartReview' in actionKeys (see plan autoDecisions: deviates from PRD D-6(2)'s requestReview because the spotlight renders enabled actions only and canRequestReview is false whenever reviewStatus exists; canRestartReview covers testStatus failed/dispatch_failed). (3) Update each named test in the same commit as its consumer: action-parity.test.ts:8 maps legacy 'Review & Test' → 'requestReview'; issueActions.no-actions-lost.test.ts:20,63 rows migrate registryKey to 'requestReview'; issueActions.test.ts:153 and the key list at :58 drop reviewTest; IssueDrawer.test.tsx:769,792 replace 'issue-action-reviewTest' expectations with the surviving actions rendered there; IssueMissionControl.test.tsx:92,103 drop the reviewTest fixtures. (4) Only after all consumers are migrated: delete the reviewTest entry (issueActions.ts:262), the 'reviewTest' member of IssueActionKey (:63), the 'preserved' member of IssueActionGroup (:76), and the 'preserved' rows of the cockpit's local GROUP_LABELS/GROUP_ORDER (IssueMissionControl.tsx:93-115). Do NOT move or export GROUP_ORDER in this item — that is registry-group-exports.

Build the shared GroupedIssueActionMenu implementing the D-3 structure

expected_outputs: typecheck completes without errors
the new structure test passes: section order, phase-primary content for two phases, danger disclosure collapsed and last, counts line, disabled-item reason tooltips

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/IssueActionMenu/GroupedIssueActionMenu.tsx rendering PRD D-3's BINDING structure from the registry + hook state, using the existing shared ContextMenu primitives (ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuDestructiveItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator from shared/ContextMenu.tsx). Props: the useIssueActions action views, sessionExtras (label/icon/onSelect/destructive entries supplied by the host surface), and the explain default (wired fully in explain-toggle). Structure top-to-bottom: header label + phase chip (deriveIssueActionPhase) + counts line ('N available now · M gated') → 'For this phase' section from getPhasePrimaryActions × current phase, enabled items only, section hidden when none → registry groups in GROUP_ORDER order (skip 'danger'), each labeled with GROUP_LABELS, empty groups hidden, disabled items rendered visible-dimmed → 'This session' section from sessionExtras → collapsed 'Danger (N available)' disclosure LAST that expands to the danger-group items. Phase-primary items ARE repeated in their home group (D-3a). kind:'destructive' items outside the danger group (purgeReview, resetToPlanned, resetSession, restartAgent) stay in their home group with destructive styling and their existing confirm gates. FR-5 (verified constraint): Radix disabled items suppress pointer events, so a disabled row renders as a NON-disabled wrapper span carrying the reason tooltip via title and aria-describedby while the row itself stays non-invocable; enabled rows carry title={description}. Add max-height:70vh + overflow-y:auto to ContextMenuContent (it has none today — shared/ContextMenu.tsx ContextMenuContent className). NFR-1: DM Sans, semantic tokens, group labels uppercase 10px muted matching the cockpit panel, --destructive only for destruction. NFR-2: Radix arrow-key navigation must traverse items; disclosure toggles with Enter/Space; visible focus states. Structure test: assert full section order for two phases (e.g. WORK_RUNNING and STUCK — STUCK leads with Recover agent / Tell agent), danger collapsed by default and last, counts line, and reason tooltips on disabled items.

items.title: Given a WORK_RUNNING fixture state, when the menu renders, it renders header + phase chip + counts line, then 'For this phase' with only enabled primaries, then non-empty registry groups in GROUP_ORDER (danger excluded), then 'This session', then the Danger disclosure last and collapsed
Given a STUCK fixture state, when the menu renders, the 'For this phase' section leads with Recover agent and Tell agent per PHASE_PRIMARY_KEYS

Given a disabled action, when the menu renders it, the row appears dimmed but visible and exposes the useIssueActions disabled-reason string via tooltip and aria-describedby, and selecting it does not invoke the action

The Danger disclosure header shows an available-count, expands and collapses with Enter and Space, and destructive items inside and outside danger render with --destructive styling and keep their existing confirm gating
ContextMenuContent applies max-height 70vh with vertical overflow scrolling, and existing consumers of the shared primitives (e.g. SessionNode context menu) keep their tests green
